title: A Letter Concerning an Unanswered Invitation
summary: Our correspondent counsels patience where an uncertain message has caused offense.
author: The Correspondent's Adviser
paragraphs: A reader writes that an invitation delivered through a mutual acquaintance has gone unanswered for three weeks. The acquaintance insists the note was received, while the intended guest says no such paper came into her hands.

It is tempting to settle the matter by deciding which witness is mistaken. That would be premature. A note entrusted to another person may be delayed, mislaid or simply delivered at a moment when its meaning is not clear.

Our advice is to write once more, directly and without reproach. State the day and place of the proposed meeting, and make it easy for the recipient to decline. A second letter should not demand an account of the first.
If no reply follows, regard silence as an answer to the invitation rather than as proof of an injury. Courtesy is best preserved when it has no debt to collect.
